thread:
ash: FYI we deployed the keystore RBAC split to APAC at 02:05 UTC and started getting a small spike in mTLS handshake rejects. Proxy 502s and keystore logs show an early DENY. Anyone seeing this?

mina: I see the spike on the dashboard for apac-prod around 02:07. Sample keystore line: 
```
2026-10-11T02:07:12Z keystore-0 INFO rbac-check: principal=svc-proxy.apac check=decrypt result=DENY reason=subjects-missing
```

jorge: That suggests the rendered RoleBinding missed the serviceaccount subjects for that cluster. Our early-authorize path returns deny before calling KMS, so KMS audit will be empty.

ops-oncall: I can patch the RoleBinding quickly. Before touching, collect artifacts: kube-audit event for the apply, keystore logs, proxy sidecar logs (peer_cert_sha256 and sni), and the rendered manifest from CI.

ash: Patching now with explicit SA subjects. Commands: 
```
kubectl --context=apac-prod -n infra apply -f /manifests/keystore/rolebinding-apac-fix.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore -n infra
```

~5m later~

mina: After the patch, handshake rejects dropped from 1.9% -> 0.2% in APAC. Recovery confirmed.

jorge: Follow-ups: 1) fix template so subjects are always fully-qualified; 2) add a canary decrypt post-apply in the RBAC pipeline that runs as the target SA; 3) change keystore to emit an "early-deny" audit stub (fields: principal, reason, sni, peer_cert_sha256, trace_id) so we have traceability even when KMS not called.

ops-oncall: Also recommend an alert: mtls_handshake_denied_rate{region="apac"} > 0.5% for 3m -> page. Runbook step 1: `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-* -o yaml`.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-512 created and linked. Attach logs and rendered manifest to PR.

ash: Thanks all, opening PR for template fix and canary job. We'll run a short blameless postmortem if we see recurrence.
